q: What carbon data do EU buyers want from a Bursa textile mill?
title: Bursa textile mill: data EU buyers ask for
short: Usually Scope 1 and 2 emissions for the mill, split by site, and a figure per kilogram or metre of fabric for the products they buy. Textiles are not CBAM goods, so this is buyer-driven Scope 3 data, built from gas, steam and electricity bills and your production register.
audience: Weaving, knitting and finishing mills in the Bursa textile cluster of Turkey supplying EU brands

ul: Scope 1: natural gas, coal or fuel oil burned in boilers and dryers.
Production for the same period, in kg or metres.
The method and factors used, so the buyer can check them.

p: Divide each site's emissions over its output using kg or metres, or machine hours where products differ a lot. State the basis next to the figure.
Textiles are outside Annex I of the CBAM Regulation. Buyers ask because their own Scope 3 includes purchased goods.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
